# Completion ledger

## Creator authority — completed implementation, 2026-10-30

Approved governance activates through the existing certified schedule unless the
verified creator explicitly signs a timely veto during bootstrap. All special
creator authority ends permanently at no more than 50 verified people, including
the creator. Legacy creator-signed activation authoring is removed. Wire version
38 / block version 9; wallet review and offline signing reuse existing actions.

Validation completed: 55 selected node regressions, 519 small-crate tests
(3 existing ignored), the extended offline veto roundtrip, 7 native wallet cases,
wallet TypeScript/native compilation, and the wire-version compatibility case.
The final node cases include ordinary verification reaching 50 followed by
revocation to 49 and restored phase encoding. Replay now latches that transition;
Epoch replay reads the permanent phase without recounting the population.

Production checkpoint/release gates remain closed; no release package rebuilt.
These focused checks do not qualify a public release or a native GUI/IPC journey.
Evidence: `target/validation-evidence/creator-authority-20261030/HANDOFF.md`.
No further implementation or focused validation is pending for this change.
VM1 is deallocated; temporary SSH access removed. No validation job is active.

### Recovery caller review after152

Read-only continuation traced the actual production caller, not only the simple
rewind wrapper. `node/src/fork_resolution.rs` calls
`rollback_plan::stage_with` for admission evaluation and elected installation.
`stage_with` consumes descendant-first journals through
`rewind_block_with_snapshots` one at a time, then calls the candidate callback.
The production callback restores payment engines after that loop. A branch
containing a Merge and a verification transition therefore does not by itself
combine topology and revocation changes into one inverse journal.

When a graph inverse cannot retain the cache, `finish_trst_rewind` leaves it
absent. Later rewind iterations return early from `prepare_trst_rewind` when
that cache is absent; they do not each reconstruct all TRST state. The subsequent
`payment_transition::restore` calls `read_trst_engine`, which performs checked
wallet/graph reconstruction on a cache miss. This source trace rules out a
full-state reconstruction per remaining journal in this reviewed loop; it does
not establish a time/memory bound or prove all generic callers avoid fallback.
The public replacement callback remains general and must not be inferred safe
solely from the production callback review.

Also inspected the retained inverse's pending-basis guard: warm validation uses
`basis_validation_changes`, reverse origin/revision indexes and dirty rows.
It is not an unconditional scan of every pending row. Cold initialization still
decodes the pending table, and a large affected dependency set still costs work.
Existing `pending_revision_basis_scaling` and retained-graph recovery drivers
cover these distinct questions. Ledger reconciliation found that the same mixed
journal caller review was already recorded with the October21 pending work;
this continuation confirms that disposition rather than claiming a new fix.
The existing pending diagnostic covers100/1k/10k/100k rows: zero unrelated warm
row decodes, exactly one dirty-row decode, orphan rejection and cold reopen.
Its latest diagnostic parent is
`/home/burst/complexity-pending-revision-basis-corrected-20261021/scale-receipt.json`;
recorded100k cold construction2.053s and median warm validation0.025645ms are

passes. Do not schedule that implementation again. Distinct dependency fanout,
large affected sets and current full-node cold recovery remain separate gaps.
Before reusing this old result for a current claim, verify its receipt inputs;
no fresh receipt verification or runtime test was performed in this review.

## Prior handoff 135: settled Receive history lookup

Source review found a remaining CX08/CX10 amplification: `prepare_settled_token`
called `basis_excludes` separately for each settled chunk, walking the same remainder
revision chain repeatedly. This is avoidable work beyond required chunk validation.
The new `basis_excludes_all` resolves all requested origins in one walk, retaining
only unresolved origin IDs; the latest revision wins, and missing/restored origins
still reject the clean basis. Entire/Single/empty semantics are unchanged. For c
chunks and h visited revisions this removes up to c*h revision lookups, using one
pass plus O(c) temporary membership state. No graph flattening or economic changes.

Historical handoff042: retirement observer contention fix PASS10storage+6node checks.
BodyChangeWatch previously held the payment-writer observer mutex across the entire
mutation callback pass (root decoding and scratch work). It now detaches rows and
the exact cut under that mutex, then runs callbacks and drops detached rows outside
it. Detached rows remain charged against the original row/byte limits. Concurrent
commits retain their images and native identities for the next visit. Callback
error/panic or committed overflow permanently invalidates coverage; aborted writes
do not. The native commit/publication lock and final cut checks remain unchanged.
This removes callback-batch work from writer lock hold time; it does not make the
required root traversal constant-time or establish measured throughput improvement.

Concrete new blocker: BodyChangeWatch::visit_commits held its mutex across every
consumer callback; payment writers acquire the same mutex in observer begin/commit.
The callbacks decode roots and write/compact scratch, so their full batch cost could
stall admission even with bounded row counts. The fix detaches rows at the checked
cut, reserves their row/byte budget until callbacks finish, retains concurrent
commits for the next visit, and poisons coverage on error/panic/committed overflow.
Native commit publication remains locked and identity-checked. No economic or
signature rule changes. This is a new production boundary, not yet qualified.

found four additional consumers that would reject a larger captured inventory:

| Reverse account planning | Active policy row allowance or legacy MAX_ROWS; complete captured count checked | Traverse all positions once in reverse account/height order, with exact observation/account agreement; no per-window head restart |

The existing account fingerprint already streams bounded pages with a terminal
completion/failure guard. SortedRecordsBuilder already streams ordered indexes
with fixed-key-width working memory. Do not replace either as if they collected
all accounts/records. Partitioning here needs bounded work/coverage and retained
storage accounting, not simply another Vec of per-partition file handles.
ScratchFile now retains an active policy for files created or grown under it,
including retained successor/catalogue files. Paths without an explicit initial
policy still need one before extending inventory capacity; resetting per-partition
byte counters cannot replace aggregate accounting. No cap was changed.

Current handoff: retirement capacity contract reconciled from source.
No source change or runtime run. The prior history-preparation-cache attempt002
remains the latest passing build. Production physical deletion stays disabled.
The R5 blocker is larger than scheduling overhead: the default30-day retention
window and the131072-row whole-inventory admission ceiling are incompatible with
sustained arrival above0.0505679bodies/s (one body per19.7754s), even assuming an
empty initial inventory, immediate certified-cut advancement and no other limits.
At1body/s the row ceiling is exceeded in131073s (36.409h), before age eligibility.
The64MiB raw-byte ceiling can bind earlier. These are body counts, not TPS.

Historical scheduling analysis (superseded by the five-check scan-scheduling pass
above): Worker::start slept the configured interval before EVERY run_cached page, not
just before a complete scan. The old default max_bodies256/interval3600 therefore gave
an optimistic deletion upper bound0.071111bodies/s; actual recovery/commit time
lowers it. With no deletions and4096examined/page, inspecting131072rows requires
at least32scheduled pages/32hours of sleep, excluding work. The rate bound was
already known; tracing the first-eligibility/inventory constraint shows why merely
shortening the interval cannot repair the capacity failure. More input capacity,
production enablement, shorter retention or weaker closure are NOT inferred fixes.

Concrete implementation order: first add bounded durable storage of *untrusted*
recovery input chunks, using the existing snapshot-page integrity/atomic-publication
pattern and scratch accounting. Reopen must verify complete extent/digest/context
metadata and reject partial/corrupt/foreign bundles. Feed reopened bytes through the
existing base/history authenticators; never deserialize an opaque authenticated
proof type. Then integrate resumable capture with explicit changed-cut handling,
bounded closure progress and deletion-writer publication checks. Retain the current
limits until the whole replacement works; a durable input cache alone does not close
R5 or remove the131072/64MiB inventory ceilings.

Cost distinction: walking a previously unauthenticated ancestry chain and checking
its signatures is required by the current head/hash-chain proof design. Persisting
raw bytes can avoid refetching and reconstruction, but is not evidence of O(1)
restart authentication. No authenticated skip-link mechanism was found in the
inspected history implementation. This review does not introduce a protocol change
or weaken signing, and does not close durable-resume or capacity gates.

Next validation boundary: new durable chunk implementation needs interrupted-write,
reopen/corruption, foreign-context and aggregate-budget cases before node integration.
Reuse retirement-promise attempt002 and retirement-reconcile receipts for their
unchanged functional scopes; no repeat live/load/release run is justified yet.

Consumer integration review (2026-10-24, source inspection; no runtime claim):
The pre-integration review found test-only BodyChangeWatch/ObservedBodyRoots callers.
Retirement-reconcile now adds the production consumer, original prefix classification,
exact commit exclusion and a monotone protected-closure index. Its production deletion
gate remains closed.
resolve_body deliberately rejects unknown hashes outside checked replay/inventory;
raw body existence cannot substitute for that authentication.

The next coherent implementation must preserve these boundaries:

- Implemented and verified in commit-identity above: bounded, environment-bound identity for each observed native commit.
  Match only the exact successful retirement commit when excluding its own
  deletions. Filtering by hash alone could hide a later delete/reinsert of that hash.
  Charge identity overhead to the existing observation budget; root-free soft
  commits must not accumulate an unbounded list of empty batches.
- Retain authenticated closure/prefix facts in private bounded scratch. New roots
  may revoke old eligibility, never grant new eligibility or infer certified prefix
  membership from a hash. Check changed/removed required bodies explicitly.
- Reconcile at the observation cut using a checked reader, then recheck under the
  deletion writer. Gaps, layout/epoch changes, missing bodies, exhausted budgets
  and interrupted reconciliation invalidate reuse. Keep the production gate closed.

R5 dependency trace: the common mutate_raw hook alone is not complete. Verification
aggregate/virtual-target replacement, governance replacement and block-group journal
publication include direct LMDB writes. UndoRecorder coalesces repeated keys and
removes A→B→A, so persisted undo is not a complete intervening-reference log. Its
existing replayed_change extractor accepts authenticated replay preparations only;
feeding arbitrary stored journals into it would remove that trust boundary.
Reconciliation therefore requires explicit coverage of typed mutation paths plus
unknown-write invalidation, not reuse based on journal presence or operation name.
All current root classes remain in bodies.rs::collect (TRST/pending, BRN, receipts,
verification, governance/delegation, frontier/confirmation, signer/round, undo,
applied replay, selection receipts). Production retirement remains gated.

R5 aggregate scratch accounting passed29focused checks (scratch-budget-20261024).
All replay temporary-file constructors now use one directory account: indexes,
variable records/sequences, recovered block bodies, snapshot bodies, canonical
sort runs and epoch sort runs. Existing live files are counted before a lease;
forks share charges. Growth reserves the complete logical extent before writing;
partial/error writes retain reservations until their file owner drops. This is
O(1) accounting per write with a shared mutex, not a filesystem quota or a measured
speedup. Filesystem allocation rounding, journal overhead and in-memory buffers
are not included. A directory-wide lease also constrains concurrent replay work
using that directory; an error defers retirement, never authorizes deletion.

Enabled retirement requires an explicit nonzero max_scratch_bytes; the default
is unset and retirement remains disabled. No invented production capacity value.
The existing small integration fixture explicitly uses64MiB. The owned async
attempt retains its lease when its caller drops the wait future, then awaits
blocking preparation/publication and existing shutdown checks.

were rewritten repeatedly. A per-reader Option<u64> now skips only identical

changes rather than message count during a same-second burst. Authentication,
message ordering, reply handling and stored liveness precision are unchanged.

## R5 single-pass closure recovery (2026-10-24)

Source review found that close_from_peers resolves every direct root to collect
missing bodies, then close_recovered resolves those roots again while walking
dependencies. Missing transitive bodies are discovered only in the second pass,
after the peer request, so they cannot be filled by that attempt. The changed
walker traverses local dependencies once and collects all missing hashes. Only
authenticated snapshot-prefix witnesses can fill them; prefix bodies remain
leaves. The complete closure is published only after every missing hash is filled.
Local and recovered bytes share the original whole-attempt budget; body and edge
limits, context checks, signatures, cut checks and production gate are preserved.

This removes duplicate local resolution, not the remaining global inventory,
root collection, all-missing request allocation or restart/persistence limits.
The new regression uses a diamond graph whose missing prefix is not a direct
root and verifies one resolution per unique body plus unchanged count rejection.
The existing sparse/full installed recovery test now checks total byte accounting.

prefixes instead of revisiting every old promise and unrelated signer namespace.

epochs and U unclosed promises, extraction decodes E+U rows plus bounded index
seek/boundary work; full journal authentication remains O(all journal rows) in
recovery and is required before constructing this reader. No skipped record is
deleted, no new signing authority is inferred, and exact-cut publication is unchanged.

## R5 closed-epoch signing evidence (2026-10-24)

The prior turn made verified progress on election identifiers. Further source
review found that paging alone cannot unblock retirement: all final promises,
including excluded losing forks from closed epochs, were treated as canonical
body dependencies forever. Canonical witness recovery cannot supply such forks.
`payment_epoch.rs::advance_snapshot_payment_epoch` preserves promises while
closing the old epoch; `meta.rs` rejects signing in a closed epoch. Installed
journal recovery authenticates every closure marker against forward descent
within installed certificate authority before retention pins its read view.

The root collector now uses that checked closure state to distinguish durable
signing evidence from live body dependencies. It does not delete promises or
counters. Unclosed promises still root their bodies; economic, rollback, replay,
frontier and work roots retain bodies independently. Only absence from the entire
completed dependency closure can make a certified old physical body eligible.
This also avoids requiring a nonexistent canonical witness for an excluded old
promise. Unknown, self-closing and backwards markers cannot authenticate a cut.

The existing retirement/reopen regression now includes an unavailable excluded
old promise, its authenticated closed epoch, and a live promise whose body must
remain required. Whole-metadata equality checks preserve both promises through
abort/stale/commit/reopen paths. The existing journal guard gains self, unknown-
target and backwards closure cases. This is a coherent semantic prerequisite to
resumable capacity work, not removal of inventory limits or production gating.

hash. The signer-root collector nevertheless requested both that identifier and
the promised block. Real nonzero election identifiers therefore obstruct closure.

recovery authentication are unchanged. The existing physical retirement/reopen
regression now inserts a real election identifier and checks that the promised
body remains required while the identifier does not. Existing metadata equality
and reopen assertions cover preservation of the promise.

## Current R5 stored witness roots (2026-10-23)

Previous goal turn made verified progress: retained planner11affected checks passed.
Current source replaces closure recovery's Vec of every account cursor and the
worker's second account map with authenticated private account/head records. Only
queried cursors and consumed account names are materialized. Records are initialized
from checked snapshot cursors, retain an immutable in-memory context/index root,
and have no deserializer/reopen API; they cannot turn unsigned disk rows into proof.
Cached stored-root lookup inspects only bounded cached requested proofs, preserves
request order and propagates storage corruption.

A related avoidable time cost is removed: after each witness chunk, the old worker
compared every wanted hash with every remaining account cursor. AccountRoots now
uses keyed head membership for both memory and stored plans, reducing that check
from O(W*A) to O(W) expected hash-table work or O(W*256) bounded index-depth work.
Consumed accounts cannot be restarted. Stored roots add disk I/O and a complete
initial account pass; this is not a measured full-node latency improvement.

Request slicing was rejected after tracing ancestry traversal: separate jobs could
repeat walks from the same head. One existing bounded request is retained. Missing
hashes, committed cursors and returned proof arrays remain under existing request
budgets; complete streamed closure, durable restart, initial staging, capacity and
sustained-write progress are still open. Account/body/byte/time caps and signing,
context, no-installation and stale-publication requirements remain unchanged.

## Retained R5 external inventory integration (2026-10-23)

batch without a helper-only build. RetainedInventory now stores observations in
ordered authenticated ScratchRecords instead of an Arc slice. Successor comparison
and full verification stream records. Body lookup authenticates a keyed record, and
retirement scans use an exclusive suffix seek through compressed Patricia paths
(at most256branches plus one leaf per index) followed by bounded pages; no prefix rescan or new
all-record descriptor list is used. Account walks retain body hashes and fetch exact
observations from the shared disk-backed inventory. Scratch read errors propagate to
candidate planning. All physical inventory/closure/byte/row caps remain unchanged.

Suffix completion describes only the requested suffix, not the skipped prefix count.
Whole scans still require the exact total count. New tests compare present/absent
key boundaries with sorted ranges, exercise compressed prefixes, paired suffixes,
last-leaf no-prefix-work, ordered construction failure, page budgets and fork/error
behavior. The existing point-lookup test now also rejects truncated scratch storage.

At this retained batch, long-lived O(N) observation ownership was removed, while
borrowed payload/hash vectors, account groups and committed cursor preparation
remained. The current retained-planner batch above supersedes those collections. Point lookup adds bounded-depth authenticated disk I/O; initial construction
adds linear scratch disk use. No large-state latency/RSS or durable-restart claim.

## Current R5 retention capacity diagnosis (2026-10-23)

Previous turn made progress: one inventory traversal and per-account height reuse
passed four affected checks. Source review now identifies a quantitative capacity
blocker, rather than another small scan optimization. Evidence is
retention-capacity-review-20261023/capacity-review.json, including hashes of actual
configuration, coordinator, inventory and design sources. No build or load run is
needed for this arithmetic. No process is being awaited or restarted.

The disabled default policy retains30days, sleeps3600seconds between completed
attempts, and deletes at most256bodies/attempt. Its optimistic deletion ceiling is
0.071111bodies/s (6144/day), before preparation, required roots, byte budget, failures
or certified-cut lag. Initial recovery rejects a physical inventory over131072rows
or64MiB including body/index bytes. At an illustrative100new bodies/s, the row ceiling
alone is reached in1310.72seconds (21.845minutes), before a30-day-old body exists.
That window admits259200000bodies; the default deletion ceiling is1406.25times lower
than arrivals even after bodies become eligible. These are physical bodies, not a
claim that user operations, blocks and decision2.2 TPS are interchangeable. Existing
rows or the byte limit can exhaust capacity sooner. Production remains gated/off.

| BodyClosureLimits131072bodies/64MiB/2Medges | Complete declared dependency closure per attempt | Resume/persist checked closure at a certified cut; no partial closure may authorize deletion |
| changes.rs replay/migration limits | Per-transition/delta preparation and undo | Keep distinct from physical history; do not raise these to work around body count |
| BodyRetirementConfig and sleep-after-run | Operator age and maximum retirement service rate | Preserve configurable policy; qualify sustained throughput, eligible fraction and disk growth with measured stage costs |
| Existing archive/history proof path | Missing-body recovery and authority | Retain proof verification, peer availability errors and restoration rights; a scratch file is not a durable archive |

Decisions10.2/10.4 choose operator policy and recoverable peer history; decision2.2

their fixture sizes, not this capacity contract. Raising caps, shortening retention,
or removing durability cannot close the identified blocker.

Next coherent implementation boundary is resumable authenticated inventory/closure
with bounded per-attempt preparation and safe progress across admitted writes. Reuse

identity, stale-root invalidation, restart and aggregate scratch-disk limits before

## Retained C16/R5 idle preparation cost (2026-10-23)

Previous turn made verified progress on outcome claim semantics. Consumer/source
review found that the periodic retirement runner repeats full recovery and closure
even after a complete empty scan with no storage change. Added an idle-generation
shortcut only after a complete no-deletion cursor cycle at one unchanged committed
generation. Each later idle tick performs a read-generation check instead of full
preparation. Any committed write, unknown generation, deletion or failed attempt
prevents/revokes skipping; a changed cut halfway through a cursor cycle cannot
qualify its unvisited earlier portion. Policy is fixed for the worker and eligibility
age is relative to the certified cutoff, so wall time alone does not change it.
The shortcut never authorizes deletion or retains pinned readers across ticks.

| run_once/commit economics unchanged; commit comment only | Physical atomicity and semantic outcomes | retirement-outcomes/crash and prior receipts | Reuse scopes; no daemon/release or broad suite |

The payment namespace batch is completed progress: build96s, five checks passed,
verified receipts/archive. Remaining signer trace found reconcile_journals doing
one metadata lookup per representative per historical anchor, even with no local
journal. This avoidable sum-of-roster-sizes probe cost is now replaced by an
index of the rows actually present in the pinned transaction.

JournalIndex reuses ScratchRecords for authenticated height heads and descending
position links, retaining only a decoded position and the existing bounded journal
decoder in memory. The index is created lazily when a journal exists; no-journal
reconciliation creates no scratch files and still validates the whole authority
stream. Each indexed row checks electorate membership before existing decode,
decision consistency and retained-tip rules. Unvisited future journals still
reject via the exact count. Durable journals are never rewritten.

For A anchors and J journals, lookup/index work is O((A+J)*d), with fixed-key trie
depth d<=256, plus J membership checks and required journal authentication.
Construction adds indexed scratch I/O and O(J*d) worst-case scratch bytes; this
is not a claim that dense/small cases are faster or that full recovery is bounded.
No history-sized signer inventory or new storage framework was introduced.

## Current C16 pinned rollback records (2026-10-23)

Consumer trace: rollback_plan uses complete BlockUndo changes and exact local
revision after-images; stage_undo derives replacement journals from authenticated
transitions and allocates revision counters only inside publication. ScratchRecords
and ScratchSequence already provide private disk-backed storage. Retaining only
hash references would lose conflict/absence semantics, so the checked-cut reader
now exposes complete decoded local journals and typed proposal counters, borrowing
one journal per callback. It uses the same pinned view as the economic readers.

The reader seeks a bounded100-row/64MiB page across whole block_undo/ and
governance_revision/ namespaces, reuses BlockUndo::decode, preserves counter zero
versus absent rows, rejects unsupported versions/noncanonical keys and poisons
on any callback/budget/decoding error. It retains one cursor and one decoded
journal, not all images. Initial full recovery remains state-sized. These are
observed local rollback records, not replay-authenticated state or deletion authority.

## Retained C16 verification-state paging (2026-10-23)

The verification-state visitor now has a key-only adapter using the existing
recovery address decoder. A separate VerificationReferenceReader borrows the
same recovery-checked view as TRST/BRN/receipt pages. It requires format2, no
legacy aggregate and a rules row; a presence-only metadata lookup avoids copying
the aggregate just to reject mixed storage. It streams the broad verification_state/
prefix, rejects legacy target/unknown-schema rows, preserves callback error types,
invalidates after errors, and uses the existing100-row/64MiB page ceilings. Counts
and cross-row membership still depend on recovered inventory validation.

transaction. RecoveredTrstReferences exposes it from the recovery-checked cut.

orphan children, misplaced headers and malformed rows. Callback errors retain

initial whole-inventory traversal is performed. Each child checks header presence
with one keyed lookup; whole inventory authentication remains the recovery guard.

## Retained C16 writer-to-reader handoff (2026-10-23)

The clean writer can now pin a TRST read view from its own environment before
releasing writer exclusion. This closes the intervening-commit gap for a future
coordinator that checks recovery evidence in that writer first. The returned
reader outlives the writer, so paging does not hold writer exclusion. Dirty,
failed, undo-active or previously changed writers are rejected; reversing an edit
does not make an uncommitted view suitable. This API does not authenticate a cut,
resolve references, or grant deletion authority. No node consumer uses it yet.

Source review: RecoveredInstalledMetadata::verify_unchanged checks the base,
certified records, retained inventory, journals, applied tail and economics.
AppliedEconomics::verify_unchanged scans accounts, restores BRN/TRST, normalizes
expiry on private copies, compares graph/holdings, pending and caches. It is not
a constant-time writer fence and must not be repeated per reference page or
reported as bounded-memory authentication. The coordinator still needs a reviewed
plan for initial authentication and bounded publication rechecks, alongside the
other C16 roots and authenticated replacement/retirement work.

## Retained C16 pinned TRST reference pages (2026-10-23)

Previous turn made progress with three typed extraction checks. The new
store_lmdb::retention::TrstReferenceReader now consumes those visitors against
real storage. It owns one pinned read transaction across bounded pages and exposes
that same view for a future coordinator to authenticate its cut. It does not
claim that raw local records, a generation number or a reference list is trusted.
No pruning coordinator or deletion path is enabled.

The scan covers stable holding rows, ancillary origin/ownership/invalidation/cause
records, normalized graph records and pending transfers. Source review found that
trst_state/v1/2..5 remain valid with stable holdings: only obsolete positional
0/1 rows are rejected. Holding header/head/next references and all WalletRecord
reference variants now have visitors. Cause blocks and origin ownership survive
spent holdings. Account references remain borrowed; reference output is streamed.

Each call processes at most 100 rows and a caller-selected encoded key/value byte
budget capped at the existing 64MiB operation bound. Range cursors resume after the
last completed key. The scan retains one cursor and decoded row, not an inventory
vector; a larger inventory requires more calls rather than a raised lifetime cap.
This is not a measured decoded-heap/RSS bound. Marker/mixed-layout, key/codec,
oversized row and callback failures invalidate the reader permanently. Callers
must discard accumulated results on error. Pending decoding uses a byte-limited,
trailing-byte-rejecting codec; the existing pending readers retain their previous
codec and share only the unchanged key parser.

## Current payment observer snapshot correction (2026-10-23)

Previous turn reconciled actual CX08 migration paths and existing cloud inventory.
Current source review of the existing payment fixture found repeated observer work:
every10ms, every pending item opens a block-height read and (when admitted) another
account read/decoding on each peer, plus a canonical read on confirmation. WithP
pending items/A accounts/N peers, account decoding and transaction setup are O(NP)
per poll even when most items share an account.

The test observer now opens one consistent read snapshot per peer, reads each
pending account once within that snapshot, and retains per-item height and exact
canonical-index checks. Account decoding is O(NA), transaction setup O(N), while
necessary pending inspection remains O(NP). No cross-poll cache, deadline, workload,
consensus logic or signature changes. This removes demonstrated test-driver
amplification, not a proven cause of the entire prior latency failure.

## Current CX08 migration reconciliation (2026-10-23)

Previous turn made progress: cached-vote source integration passed13 node guards;
no unfinished process is being restarted. This turn traced the remaining positional
migration item to `trst_storage::migrate`, the holder-context conversion primitive,
installed replay projection and `node/recovery_publication.rs`.

The generic startup migration deliberately returns false for positional histories
with provisional blocks. Partial row journals alone do not prove historical full
portfolio cuts or cross-account order. The converter requires caller-proven cuts;
it is not missing a simple invocation. Authenticated installed recovery already
calls `project_token_indexes_with_stable_holdings`, regenerates provisional journals,
and atomically publishes marker/holdings/journals. The historical five-configuration
migration test covers aggregate, positional and stable recovery plus both conversions,
including staged abort, commit and rewind (trst-certified-migration-host-20261020,
9.56s within23 passing checks). Later startup publication/crash proofs retain their
recorded scope; this source review is not a fresh candidate runtime pass.

Disposition: keep noncertified positional provisional conversion open; never infer
order from matching after-images. Do not invent an easier compatibility policy or
silently call the primitive. A complete solution needs authenticated historical
cuts/order for those histories, or an explicit supported-upgrade policy. Existing
certified conversion must not be rebuilt as if absent. No code/test execution was
needed for this reconciliation. CX01/CX08 current decision rows now summarize the
actual latest evidence instead of prescribing superseded queue/storage diagnostics.
Historical failures and full objective remain unchanged.

Legacy policy clarification is pending with the user: require the implemented
certified recovery/resync path when context is absent, or additionally support
automatic in-place migration for those legacy histories. No answer is assumed,
and no dependent compatibility policy/code change is authorized by elapsed time.

## Current cached-vote read snapshot correction (2026-10-23)

Cached soft/final response revalidation now opens a committed read snapshot,
not the exclusive ledger writer. Extracted guard reads remain verbatim identical

fence and requires rejection. It checks sequence preservation and no intervening
transaction generation. Existing malformed/epoch/fence/governance/choice guards
remain. This proves read-cut semantics, not freshness beyond that cut; previously
issued signed bytes are replayed, never a new promise authorized by stale state.

## Current R1 duplicate ingress correction

Previous diagnostic made progress: actual heap residence dominated the failed
block's admission delay. Rechecked saved logs show1216 of2370 dequeues after the
same node's durable publication;1163 estimated enqueue times were after publication
by more than1ms. That enqueue estimate mixes wall-clock logging with monotonic
residence and is not an exact race boundary. Evidence:
`admission-residence-host-20261023/downloaded/load12/durable-duplicate-analysis.json`.

Two production files now remove redundant ingress work. Network block admission
checks the same stored-block condition already used by the validation worker,
before consuming queue/retention capacity; failed reads still go through normal
validation. No long-lived rejection cache, and rollback permits later retries.
The queue uses a bounded ordered index of Blake2b-256 digests over the complete
serialized payload, including signature, work and content. Identical queued
payloads share one entry/retention slot; all three pop paths remove the key so
later dependency retries remain eligible. Different same-hash signatures/work/
content remain separate candidates. Coalescing grants no authentication or finality.
Cost is O(payload bytes + log Q) per push; index space O(Q), not retained history.

Existing full-capacity tests now submit distinct payloads to test actual capacity;
limits and assertions remain. Added regressions cover altered signature/work/
content, invalid-signature-first arrival, retry after each dequeue path, returned
recovery retention slots, and stored-block retry after deletion/rollback.

## Current R1 scheduler correction: indexed queue and bounded drain

Saved private-RAM logs show102 primary-node accepted events during the failed
block's18.427s queue-to-admission window. Median durable-commit event elapsed8.096ms
versus123ms accepted-event elapsed; grouped publications share some starts, so
these are not additive stage timings or proof that one lock caused the delay.
Analysis: `multi-account-load-host-20261022/downloaded/ram-private/postcommit-analysis.json`.

Source inspection found avoidable queue costs: `PriorityScheduler` used a sorted
Vec with linear duplicate search, insertion, removal and front pop. A full drain
could be quadratic. Two bounded ordered indexes now make individual push/pop/
remove O(log Q), retaining descending balance, duplicate-root identity and strict
higher-priority replacement at capacity. Zero capacity now retains nothing.
Equal-balance order was unspecified and is now deterministic hash order; this is
the election scheduler, not the PoW ingress queue. PoW policy remains unchanged.

The node previously held the scheduler mutex across ledger reads and async
rebroadcast/election locks. It now locks only for queue mutation. Drain examines
at most256 entries per tick, including corrupt/stale entries, rather than bounding
only successful elections. Remaining work stays queued and durable backlog scanning
continues. New regressions cover stale-page progress and queue availability while
an election writer is unavailable, plus index consistency after eviction/remove/
clear/reinsert. This does not yet establish a sustained-load latency improvement.

## Current R1 repair: replay final signatures before local cementation

The volatile trace shows final signing followed by soft responses for the same
block while other peers are still waiting. `respond_vote` selected final responses
only after local confirmation height advanced; an already final signer could
therefore create another soft response during repair. Final votes are sticky in
elections, so this does not demonstrate an equivocation or finality violation.
It does waste repair work and withholds an available final signature from peers.

`node/src/durable_votes.rs` now selects the existing cached final response before
cementation through `generate_vote(..., true)`. Current dependencies, candidate
hash, durable reservation, epoch and governance fences are still checked. It does
not promote a block without an existing final signature. The existing regression
asserts final response bytes/sequence remain identical while confirmation height
is still1, before advancing it to2. Cache eviction/restart behavior is unchanged.

Admission grouping source review found two necessary implementation boundaries:
LmdbWriteTransaction currently permits exactly one undo journal, and admission
publishes live/frontier state before validating the next block. A group needs
separate per-block before-values plus a staged admission view; clearing dirty or
moving commit outside the loop is unsafe. BlockValidationQueue has cancellation-safe
single delivery but no ready-group operation, and the one-worker case has no
lookahead after delivery. RwTxn cannot cross awaits in the current Send worker future.
Implement storage journal grouping and the caller coherently, bounded by items/bytes,
without waiting to fill or reordering shutdown/checkpoint/fork controls. Existing
undo, prepared-rebase, cancellation and admission-fault regressions are the test base.

## Retained R1/R4: release selection integrated;72 component and9 node checks passed

Signing-state source trace reaches account_info, which waits on the live BRN mutex
while calculating spendable balance and selecting returned-stake proofs, then
block_info for the predecessor odometer/grant. Ordinary commit retains that mutex
through durable staging and publication. Existing preparation timings do not split
RPC wait, server work and signing, so no unique cause of the multi-second tails is
established. No signing/grant checks or publication locking were removed.

The trace found a separate algorithmic gap: release_sources selected from every
pending row, including empty unproven proofs. PendingReleases now maintains a shared
ordered map of nonempty proofs, with the same Arc payloads as authoritative rows.
Selection visits only that map in the original outcome order. Insert, replacement,
removal and decoding maintain it; canonical serialization still emits only rows.
The prior nonempty count is replaced by the map's length. Empty proofs retain their
amounts and rights in authoritative storage; they simply cannot contribute hashes.

For R pending rows and P nonempty proofs, selection no longer visits R-P empty
rows. It can still visit all P nonempty proofs when greedy whole-proof selection
cannot fill a block. Derived storage adds O(P) tree entries sharing payloads;
updates add O(log P) path work, and cold loading rebuilds the index. This is not a
constant-time selection or measured small-fixture payment speedup.

## Current R4: ordered lifecycle origin snapshots integrated;30 focused checks passed

R4 source review found wallet-wide revoke/restore collecting all origin IDs into
Vec and sorting even though wallet_origins is SharedSet<TxHash> backed by OrdSet,
and TxHash derives byte-array Ord. Both paths now retain the shared ordered root.
Restoration clears wallet flags first, snapshots remaining outcome holds and lazily
filters those origins, preserving the independent-hold rule. Named receipt-origin

Governance finding: apply_governance_record_delta advances one local u128 revision
per touched proposal; pending effects retain global aggregate ownership. Recovery
stage_caches can advance revisions before journal installation. Physical recovery
journals therefore need a bounded, checked revision allocation/rebase in that same
writer after publication, applied consistently to overlapping proposal histories.
Do not copy replay counters, reset revisions, omit guards or trust old journal
state images. This remains implementation work, not a newly invented economic rule.

Provisional normalization review (2026-10-22, source evidence, no new run):
BlockUndo::decode caps one journal at65536 changes and64MiB, whereas recovery
scratch MAX_ROWS is131072. UndoRecorder::record/preview_verification_change also
reserve1024 bytes and account for existing composed before-images. Therefore a
normalized delta that fits the recovery scratch is not necessarily a valid block
journal. Current apply_verification_record_delta validates each physical old row,
previews the complete existing recorder budget, clears pending physical rows on
overflow, and promotes to the original aggregate image. Rules changes or an
already aggregate-owned verification scope retain that global boundary. A new
recovery normalizer must reuse these semantics, not duplicate a loose row cap.

Governance record deltas also advance governance_revision/v1/<proposal> through
ordinary journaled put_meta. Those revisions reject later changes within the same
proposal even when a different ballot key changed. Recovery currently reconstructs
global governance images and does not derive these local revision images. Simply
emitting GovernanceRecord deltas would omit that guard. Revision values are local
storage guards, not signed proposal contents; do not invent them from ledger data
or reset them without proving all staged/current journal and candidate boundaries.

| Required normalization boundary | Concrete next action / evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Whole block budget, not isolated lifecycle delta | Arrange physical-delta selection after other block changes are known; expose/reuse existing recorder budget/promotion machinery. Cover exact row/byte boundary and mixed physical/global composition. |
| Verification rules / formats | Capture and recheck v1/v2 mode at pinned source and publication writer. Keep rules changes and oversized deltas aggregate-owned; no mixed physical/aggregate ownership. |
| Governance proposal revision guards | Trace and reconstruct guard before/after images against the pinned writer, or retain aggregate conflict scope. Prove same-proposal conflict rejection and independent-proposal preservation after recovery/reopen. |
| Signed provisional scenario | Extend installed_recovery's payment_delta_recovery pattern using selection::setup_with and Fixture::push signatures, with ordinary governance staging; compare recovered rollback with original admission. Existing confirmed signed192 queries cannot prove this. |
| Final publication and budget compatibility | Keep the typed publishers and canonical logical byte charges already validated. Normalization must not lower accepted-state limits merely by counting a former logical row as thousands of physical rows. |

account state. Saved ordering: Burn817cb683… prepared between21:27:45.499 and45.559;
preceding Receivec0657d6e… was not admitted on origin36143 until46.369. The burn

Source explains the supported cause:rpc::handlers::handle_process waits at most2s
for a submission result and intentionally reports accepted=true for Queued too.
payment_load::publish treats that as durable admission and immediately calls
signed_block for the next account operation; signing_state queries the current
account_info head. This can create an actual competing block while the predecessor
is still queued. The production SDK submit_ready_block_with_content already waits
for exact signed-block confirmation before returning; this finding is in the
pipelined raw-process load fixture, not proof that the SDK bypasses that guard.

Smallest correction: before the fixture signs the next operation for an account,
observe exact predecessor admission (not finality), while retaining the existing
25s budget from original submission for final confirmation. Register the pending
sample immediately so admission waiting remains included in observed latency.
Do not serialize on finality, relax rejection assertions, extend deadlines, or
reinterpret queued acceptance as durable. Add a deterministic queued-response
regression using existing test infrastructure before another load. Preserve fixture
/tmp/.tmp7WnjU5 and the earlier /tmp/.tmphrY7xd; no new ledger generation for diagnosis.

## Current CX11: wallet-record codec groundwork — three tests passed

The full-row locality trace found two independent journal producers: live storage
and authenticated checkpoint replay (`changes/recorded.rs`). Recovery captures and
installs complete BrnWallets rows, reconstructs provisional journals, verifies

alone would make replay-produced undo disagree with physical state.

uses persistent-tree differences and serializes changed proofs only. Pauses still

allocates no capacity from untrusted counts, requires ordered complete inventories,
and preserves the old malformed-proof fallback and overflow accounting.

## Prior R5: persistent rate activation passed BRN component checks

Rate segments now use a persistent vector and cumulative accrual a timestamp-keyed
persistent map. Shared activation copies O(log R) tree paths; same-time changes select

checks both candidate/current as append-only extensions of the captured cut, copies

reinterpretation. Revocation/revision/ownership/expiry changes remain barriers.

candidate-derived holder/revision indexes are never trusted. Persistence uses the

## Prior R1 account reservations: five focused checks passed

The bounded preparation queue now reuses ParallelBlockProcessor account locks.
Only the first queued candidate for an account prepares speculatively. Its queued
siblings share the reservation through admission, so releasing the first candidate
cannot let a later worker race an earlier sibling's serial fallback. Dequeue never
awaits these locks; FIFO delivery and cancellation retention remain intact. Lock
and weak-reservation maps are reclaimed and bounded by the worker count. Busy
candidates still use normal serialized admission, which now restores authoritative
payment state before staging so skipped capture cannot bypass snapshot faults.

## Prior R1 BRN prepared-state primitive: focused check passed

Dependency review found BRN persist_brn_delta relies on serialized caller locks;
it does not compare stored before-images. TRST stable holdings/graph writers use
row CAS, but that checks changed rows, not all read-only dependencies. Publishing
whole staged roots would still discard unrelated commits even if storage CAS passed.

It copies current persistent roots, validates declared wallet reads and every changed
wallet before-image, and applies only prepared wallet changes. Any mismatch returns
an error without changing inputs. Rate history and stake-ID allocation remain
conservative global barriers. The caller must supply all read-only wallet inputs;
this API alone proves neither complete dependency tracking nor parallel safety.

## Prior R1 admission review: implementation gap confirmed

Decision25.7 and completion-plan C14 require independent-account parallel economic
preparation. Source review confirms only authentication is parallel: node.rs drains
one authenticated candidate, then holds live BRN/TRST locks through preparation,
LMDB persistence and publication before advancing its loop. economic_candidate::stage
couples writer reads, predecessor/signing-grant checks, pending consumption, engine
preparation and block-row writes. This is an implementation gap as well as missing
throughput evidence; the audit's R1 row now says so explicitly.

The existing signed Send scaling probe excludes this queue/consensus boundary.
Existing certified challenge-expiry setup already performs signed Burn/Receive/Merge
through RPC and waits for peer confirmation. Its source is a reusable fixture,
not new current-candidate performance evidence. No expensive scenario or build was
started in this review. Previous dashboard worker is terminal and its13 passes
remain the latest node/RPC boundary.

## Retained R3 revision-bearing undo: components and signed integration passed

Source reachability review found a real reversible case. Production
verification_transition::apply_staged calls verification_commit::collect_staged.
Collect defers upheld challenges and all appeals to agreed settlement, but a
certified verification vote can emit VerificationComplete. For a previously
revoked wallet, verify_wallet calls un_revoke_by_origin, appending graph revisions
and restoring affected holdings inside the ordinary block writer. Its undo is
therefore not dismissible as a finalized-only path. Outcome-invalidated origins
also change their wallet_revoked flag, while their independent causes remain.

Added a private RevisionIndex counting revisions by merge and graph references
from predecessor revisions, current heads and source composition bases. Cold
construction and retained append/revocation/removal successors maintain it by
persistent deltas. Added graph-only inverse support for fixed-topology metadata:
contributions/revoked markers, current heads and removal of appended revisions.
It compares old records, reuses the contribution proof without presuming revision
deletion valid, then rejects surviving graph references to deleted revisions.
Existing topology-changing append undo remains separate.

## Retained R3 checked graph removal: signed replacement validated

Implemented a retained inverse for complete appended graph rows. It compares all
node/source/contribution/source-basis/reverse-edge records with the validated cut,
rejects surviving downstream consumers, and preserves independent later siblings.
Exact durable edge bytes are checked by the existing journal CAS before the
logical graph proof; durable positions may have gaps, while child occurrences and
order remain exact. Affected parent edge lists are rebuilt in O(parent fanout),
which was the residual addressed by the subsequent indexed-edge change above.

Private retained indexes now include merges referenced by historical revisions
(including headless history) and original composition IDs of revoked holdings.
These prevent node deletion from orphaning records omitted by the active-holder
index. Revision-bearing removals and unsupported graph edits keep the existing
full-restoration fallback. Ordinary forward paths update the private proof indexes.
The writer prepares against a clean validated cut only after every journal image
matches, keeps ordinary raw invalidation, and publishes the successor only after
all rewind writes and journal deletion succeed. Failure poisons the writer.

## Current R2 sparse scope lookup: scoped validation passed

The previous turn completed borrowed membership reuse. This turn addressed the
remaining ~10–11s measured scope encoding/hash cost in sparse shared cuts.
RecordIndex derives a complete temporary lookup from actual canonical scope
records, structurally decodes each bounded value and recomputes its storage key.
Any malformed, mis-keyed or oversized record, or exceeded budget, disables the
whole shortcut. It never trusts outgoing/incoming discovery rows for absence.
Invalid signatures remain indexed hits and fail at the original authentication
point. Owner/chain and scope errors remain at their original lookup point.

The index borrows payloads, caps scanned input rows at16,384 and applies an8MiB
accounting budget including payload/key/table allowance; this is not a process-RSS
cap. Only shared cuts with metadata.len <= electorate.len and the row cap attempt
it, once after proposal existence is checked. Single projections, large/dense
inventories and uncertain records retain the original keyed path. No schema,
signature rules or historical authority semantics changed.

## R2 diagnosis retained: unrelated-commit invalidation confirmed

The diagnosis below preceded the implementation and results above. Its source
finding is retained; its proposed work is superseded by the current handoff.

`rpc/src/governance_projection_cache.rs::Context` keys by complete LMDB generation.
`project_until` clears every result on a generation change. In contrast,
`store_lmdb/src/write_batch.rs` carries governance and auxiliary roots from the
matching base generation and republishes them at the committed generation even
when their contents are unchanged. `node/src/governance_read.rs` forwards the new
view generation. Thus an unrelated managed payment can preserve every tally input
but force the next due proposal query to recount. This is a confirmed source-level
invalidation path, not a measured latency claim. Known-generation same-input tests
prove present behavior, not cross-generation semantic reuse.

A cache fix must preserve identity of all relevant inputs, not merely proposal
hash or governance roots: delegation, verified membership, parameters and time
boundary also matter. The current typed-cache invalidation hooks are the existing
mechanism to extend. Do not add a persistent protocol revision or keep a second
unbounded copy of engines/electorate just for result-cache comparison.

| Input / path | Existing guard found | Required next assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Governance rows, format and aggregate undo | write_batch raw mutation drops governance cache; keyed delta can install after root | Changed vote/proposal and rewind must miss |
| Delegation snapshot | AuxiliaryCache::invalidate removes matching snapshot | Delegation/revocation must miss |
| Verified electorate | Membership-aware updates preserve unchanged roots; raw account mutation clears electorate | Balance-only writes may hit; membership changes and rollback miss |
| Unknown/external writer or pinned old read | Generation matching gates typed cache access | Unknown identity bypasses; old reader cannot alias later state |
| Parameter hash and deadline | Existing RPC context and per-entry deadline checks | Keep exact boundary/backward-clock behavior |
| Cache retention | 128 entries / 8 MiB serialized proposal payload | Preserve bounds; identity metadata must not retain historical graph/electorate roots |

The identity fix and current validation status are recorded above. Do not repeat
the earlier diagnosis or its completed component checks.

invalidation path. This synchronous method invokes no external callbacks.

## Prior CX08/CX15 retained selection/period integration: 370 library and 51 selected node passes

Explicit retained selection now resolves requested IDs directly, preserving signed
order, repeated IDs for the existing validator, and the first missing-input error.
Automatic retained selection range-seeks past expired effective timestamps and examines
at most 256 active entries in (effective timestamp, token ID) order, applying the same
oldest-plus-period/10 cutoff. Raw malformed/duplicate portfolios retain existing behavior.
The active index is re-keyed by effective time rather than saturated expiry time; this
reuses the same index storage and preserves ordering when many deadlines saturate.
Expiry flush/candidate metadata translate effective time through the current period.
Governed-period rebuild, insert/remove/replace maintain the index. No encoded fields,
merge limit, eligibility or economic rule changed.

Expected retained selection work: explicit O(m log t); automatic O(log t + m log t),
m <= 256, including payload lookups. Saturating clock MAX produces no unexpired rows;
period zero and clock-before-origin behavior match the raw selector. New differential
checks cover populations around the cap, state mixes, ties, saturated effective times,
all clock/period extremes, passed-period mismatch, mutation and governed resurrection,
without materializing canonical holdings. This is source complexity, not throughput.

## Prior CX07/CX08 retained token counters: 366 library and 50 selected node passes

Implemented persistent nonrevoked timestamp-prefix sums plus revoked face totals in
`holding_rows/indexed/counters.rs`. Compressed radix nodes retain min/max/subtree sums;
paths have at most 64 branches for u64 deadlines, with one leaf per distinct timestamp
and one node per split. Zero-amount buckets retain multiplicity/deadlines. Checked
256-bit internal sums permit u128 overflow to disappear after removal; if a requested
counter exceeds u128, the API falls back to the original ordered scan so its exact
first overflow error remains unchanged. Existing raw/context-mismatch fallback remains.

Retained insert/remove/replace and governed-period rebuild maintain these counters.
`token_counter_window` uses a matching root directly before the weak-root cache, with
arbitrary signed-clock prefix/next-deadline queries and no Vec materialization. Expired
and Pending nonrevoked tokens participate by timestamp, matching the existing scan;
active-only expiry metadata is not substituted for this semantics. Snapshot encoding
and authoritative balances are unchanged. New index memory/cold-update costs need
measurement; no release/whole-payment bound claimed from source complexity.

scan; wide overflow recovery and zero deadlines; retained versus raw windows through
period/state/backward-clock changes without materialization; exact overflow fallback
and recovery after removal. 838 source inputs verified, four changed/new files.

The engine portfolio now wraps an unchanged canonical layout plus an optional retained
indexed root. Legacy immutable field access lazily materializes the canonical Vec;
mutable access drops the indexed proof before exposing the fields. Indexed clones
retain tree roots without cloning a previously materialized Vec. Serialization delegates
to the canonical layout; deserialization restores raw data and does not forge a proof.

persistent diffs without materializing the Vec. Private order labels are not canonical.

canonical bytes, mutable-proof invalidation, repeated engine debit and delta without
Vec materialization, and corruption rejection before callbacks.

## CX08 persistent holding root: proportional splits; ten component tests passed

Indexed proportional split is now implemented with the existing `basis_cut` and
`reduced_basis` graph functions and deterministic `split_token_id`. It traverses only
the merge origin's holdings, preserves active/expired remainders and original tie order,
creates revoked chunks after existing timestamp ties, and returns new portfolio and
graph roots together. Input graph and portfolio are immutable on errors, including a
late invalid remainder basis or a generated chunk-ID collision. Caller authorization
of the taint and atomic publication with pending transfers remain mandatory. Local
holding work is O(q log t) plus graph-basis/revision traversal, deterministic ID work
and O(q) events; graph ancestry cost has not been declared constant or removed.

validation boundary at one holder/governed period. Cold conversion checks the existing
snapshot invariants, owner and exact governed expiry minimum, then builds persistent
ID/order/active-expiry indexes. Checked insert/replace/remove return a new root;

identity or rejecting a payment. The exceptional relabel is O(t log t); normal point
updates perform O(log t) persistent index work. Canonical Vec export is explicitly O(t).

validation, authentication and finality remain separate requirements. The component
was not wired into engine mutations or node payments at that component boundary.

## CX08 partial-journal converter evidence: three tests passed

`block_undo::stable::convert` now converts one canonical positional journal using a
caller-supplied after-portfolio provider. It validates input identity/count/order with
the existing BlockUndo decoder, groups holding changes by owner, reconstructs each
before-portfolio with the prior scoped helper and emits stable deltas. Block hash,
account and height are preserved; nonholding changes remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
Input aggregate snapshots or existing stable rows are rejected rather than mixed.
The returned before-portfolio map covers only affected owners and is returned only
with a fully validated converted journal. No database or marker is written.

Output uses existing 65,536-change/64-MiB journal limits, charges encoded new changes
before retaining them, sorts canonical table/key order and revalidates the completed
journal. A caller-selected context budget cannot exceed 64 MiB; returned owned
portfolio sizes reduce the remaining budget before processing another owner, and
each temporary positional map is bounded by that remainder. These are encoded-data
bounds, not exact RSS accounting. Migration-wide retained-journal and work budgets
still belong to the coordinator. Nonholding payloads are preserved, not newly
semantically authenticated by this representation converter.

## CX08 independent rollback evidence: 181 storage tests passed

Migration review found an avoidable conflict in the new physical format: a payload
update and a later ordering-link update share one stable holding row. Likewise an
append changes header count even when it leaves transferable/expiry caches unchanged.
Whole-row undo comparison would reject an otherwise disjoint earlier change. Prior
reverse-order recovery tests did not exercise this case.

Added key-bound stable-row undo reconciliation. All before/after/current values must
decode under the same primary key/version. For each field changed by the journal,
the live value must still equal its after-image; rewind restores its before-image.
Unchanged fields retain their live values. Holding token payload is one indivisible
field (not per-token-field merging), separate from its next link. Header count, head,
transferable cache and expiry cache are checked individually. Creation/deletion still
require exact-row comparison. Errors leave UndoChange unmodified; no hook is granted
to primary ledger/signer records. Normal transaction preflight/abort remains intact.

New matcher regression covers disjoint payload/link and count/cache updates in both
directions, overlapping conflicts and missing images. New real journal regression
records an earlier payload debit, commits a later expired-token append, then rewinds
the earlier block: exact holdings retain the append and restore the payload/cache.
This is a storage mutation fixture, not proof that every such pair is independently
admissible under protocol dependency/finality rules. Those rules remain unchanged.

Further source trace changes the next integration plan:

* `metadata.rs::project_token_indexes_at` derives economic changes **before** opening
  its publication write transaction, then rechecks recovered evidence. Representation
  must be an explicit derivation choice carried into the projection and checked against
  the publication cut, not an unchecked later marker read. At that review boundary code remained v1; the format-carrying integration above now passes its selected tests.
* `changes.rs::derive` already holds normalized before/after TRST engines for each
  signed replay step. Generate stable deltas there with the existing row/retained/work
  budgets (131,072 / 64 MiB / 256 MiB), preserving ordering and the one cache clock.
  Do not infer missing historical neighbor IDs from an unrelated current wallet.
* `Rows::stage_caches` currently calls v1-only `stage_replayed`, and
  `metadata.rs::stage_undo` subsequently invokes aggregate-to-v1 conversion. State
  staging, journal encoding and format marker must select the same representation in
  one transaction; neither can be switched independently.
* `finality::reconcile` filters cemented blocks and normalizes surviving account
  confirmation heights after the writer recheck. Preserve that behavior and all
  `JournalGuard` checks; physical-format migration must not grant rollback authority.
* `recorded::compare_full_projection` filters through `recorded::owns`, which covers
  recorded account/index/lifecycle rows, **not TRST holding row namespaces**. It is
  insufficient proof of stable journal correctness. Add explicit applied stable-row
  restoration/rewind assertions, including linked ties and unrelated account histories.
* Existing positional journals cannot be converted by the current `convert_undo`
  function alone: only aggregate images contain their entire portfolio context.
  Signed replay can supply context in compact recovery; startup routes without that
  recovery context still need a supported conversion path. Do not drop journals or
  impose a journal-free restriction to activate stable storage.

## Current CX08 stable holding codec: four tests passed; integration/activation pending

New `trst::engine::holding_rows` defines a separate `trst_holdings/v2/` codec:
portfolio header stores count/head/caches; holding rows are keyed by holder/token
ID and carry the next token ID. Tokens and canonical WalletPortfolio serialization
are unchanged. Encoding rejects duplicate IDs/unordered or invalid cached snapshots;
row decoding binds version/key/holder with existing row/key byte limits. Scoped
restoration checks every supplied row, count, missing/cyclic/disconnected links,
owner, exact ordering and governed expiry; declared count never controls allocation.
At this codec evidence boundary no reader or marker was changed. The subsequent
reader/cache integration is recorded above; migration/replay activation remains pending.

Delta generation validates both portfolios, compares ID-keyed payload/next links,
and preserves deterministic output order. It requires O(old+new holdings) work and
O(old holdings) temporary lookup space; output allocation is O(changed rows). Front
insert/delete should change two total rows, append/middle operations up to three,
regardless of wallet length. This addresses durable row amplification only; Vec
COW/movement and the full comparison remain unresolved under the broader goal.

Four new tests cover 32/256/1024 holdings with front/tie/tail insertion, front/middle/
tail deletion and payload change; apply each delta using old-value CAS semantics,
compare full stable rows, and restore byte-identical portfolios. Other cases cover
empty versus absent portfolios, tie order unlike token-ID order, reverse deltas,
malformed topology/count/owner/caches/duplicates and key/version/trailing-byte bounds.
These are codec tests, not authentication or database/journal qualification.

## Current CX08 positional holding storage: exact cost diagnostic passed; redesign open

Source trace confirms v1 holding keys encode vector positions; reconstruction
requires contiguous positions. `persist_delta` encodes both old/new rows, compares
the persisted old value, then writes/deletes every changed positional row. Inserting
an older token shifts a suffix even though token identities do not change. Existing
record-delta tests cover two-token correctness but do not assert scaling counts.

A focused regression extends that test module at 32/256/1024 holdings. It compares
append, front insertion, oldest-timestamp tie insertion and front deletion, counts
holding-row changes and old+new encoded bytes, and applies/restores each delta
against full canonical records. Expected v1 counts are 1, n+1, n and n respectively.
This test documents the existing cost; it is not a passing performance target.
No production/storage format has changed. Sparse CX06 overhead remains open.

## Current CX06 stopped-prefix diagnosis: complete; memo write costs isolated

The two-attempt checkpoint now has an optional instrumented pass in the existing
probe. cfg(test) counters time memo reads (including returned value clone), loader
and memo writes (including owned key/result clone and Vec resize), with operation
counts. Lookup is extracted into an equivalent helper; production algorithm and
scope behavior are unchanged. Vec capacities and HashMap capacity are logged
separately from logical slots. Instrumented pass follows the ordinary paired pass;
clock overhead, allocator state and untimed control/output work prevent exact
attribution to the ordinary total. Equality and one base load per node still apply.

Caller mapping from source inspection:

| Root condition | Existing production behavior | What the synthetic stopped probe means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No proposal/parameter scoped record | Outer grants.get returns None; Walk skipped, legacy fallback preserved | Not represented by invoking Walk with Stop(None) |
| Explicit selected-scope revocation | Outer Some(None) enters Walk; hop stops without ID or ballot lookup | Represents this traversal overhead, excluding scope lookup and projection insertion |
| Grant with ineligible recipient | Hop stops before grant ID and key ballot | Represents stop result, excludes prerequisite derivation/eligibility cost |
| Valid grant with immediate effective key ballot | Hop authenticates recipient/ID then returns first choice | Stop(Some) has same cache structure; current probe uses Stop(None) |
| Missing scope reached by an incoming chain | Hop stops, without legacy fallback for the upstream owner | Represented as a terminal; its own outer query may be skipped in production |

Therefore the stopped/sparse timing cannot be generalized to ordinary absent-scope
voters. Explicit revocation can potentially bypass Walk after the existing scoped
lookup while preserving project_key_ballot(None), but no such change is made before
reconciling the diagnostic. Full projection still needs separate measurements.

## Current CX06 lazy authenticated prefixes: 32 node checks passed

`key_delegation/walk.rs` lazily caches powers-of-two hop prefixes. A query requests
only segments within its remaining budget; composition stops at the first ballot
or stopped path. Each base hop loads once per cut, retaining recipient-before-ID
and ballot ordering through the original grant cache. Outer scoped-grant lookup
still precedes each query, including depth zero, preserving absent/revoked and
legacy fallback behavior. Cycles compose finite prefixes without new metadata
loads; budget exhaustion returns no vote. Recursion depth is at most usize::BITS.
For Q queries, V reached nodes and L=floor(log2(d))+1 (d>0), at most V*L prefix
slots and O((V+Q)*L) expected map operations replace O(Q*min(d,V)) repeated hops;
outer scope work is additional. Address clones/storage and default-depth constants
need workload measurements; no performance win is claimed before measurement.

Tests added: all 2,401 four-node graphs with two ballot choices, mixed depths and
both owner orders; once-only base loads and prefix-storage bound; no metadata load
past a budget or first vote; cycles at usize::MAX; authenticated three-node cycle,
ballot and revocation states across all eligibility masks/depths/query orders
against the legacy loop. The generic helper requires immutable callback inputs.

restoration and implementation decisions 20.6–20.8. The audit now records the exact

remote depth-setting exploit is claimed. No depth clamp or semantic change made.

## Current CX06 selective terminal retention: four probes passed; cycle correction and 23 node checks passed

The measured memo cost is addressed by retaining terminals only when reached
through an incoming delegation path. Direct terminal queries return without memo
insertion. No incoming-index construction or history scan is added. A terminal
queried before its incoming path may be examined twice; once reached through a
path it is cached. Nonterminal expansion stays once per reached node. Thus Q
queries and V reached eligible nodes require O(Q+V) work, with no memo storage for
isolated terminals. This deliberately replaces the earlier strict once-per-node
implementation claim with a bounded terminal recheck, preserving the linear
complexity target and economic semantics. Exhaustive graph equality remains;
its work assertion includes only the possible extra eligible-terminal checks.
A new terminal-first/repeated-query test asserts exact lookups and retained entries.

## Current CX06 electorate commitment reuse: 195 library and 45 node tests passed

BallotElectorate binds an immutable borrowed/owned voter list to a lazily computed
canonical commitment. It preserves the legacy domain, u32 count and sorted unique
public-key encoding; duplicates and invalid addresses remain errors. Lazy validation
keeps proposal/history/delegation error precedence. The original prepare_ballot_cut
API borrows its supplied slice through this object without an extra voter-list copy.

ConfirmedReplay now prepares one owned electorate lazily after panel deadlines and
reuses it while preparing all due ballots, before applying any result or activation.
Single-ballot calls use a fresh local object. Unvoted closures return before scanning
accounts or constructing an electorate. For q voted proposals at one cut, account
collection and commitment work become one O(W + U log U) pass rather than q passes;
per-proposal tally work remains. Cache lifetime is one preparation window and retains
O(U) voters plus one hash, not historical cuts. Node integration is now verified below; workload limits remain unqualified.

New library regression independently encodes the legacy canonical electorate,
compares receipts, checks lazy guards and rejects duplicate/invalid voters. A node
fixture compares shared versus individual ballot receipts and voter allocation
identity across two proposals; it will run at the node stage.

## Current CX06 ordinary suffix resolution: 194 library and 44 node tests passed

Ordinary vote tallying now owns a BallotResolver for one immutable proposal,
parameter/category, delegation graph and eligibility set. It memoizes terminal
addresses with visit distance, or invalid paths for cycles/ineligible intermediates.
Each reached eligible node's outgoing edge is selected at most once across the tally.
The existing depth acceptance rule still counts the terminal visit; depth zero
returns no delegate. Direct owner votes and explicit key-ballot overrides stay
outside ordinary resolution, and intermediate direct votes do not truncate a chain.

The aggregate resolver may discover a suffix beyond one owner's allowed depth,
then reject that owner by stored distance. Discovery remains within the fixed
eligible graph (at most U nodes), uses no authenticated metadata and changes no
error visibility. Expected traversal work is O(U+V) hash/map operations for V reached
eligible nodes (plus underlying persistent-map lookup costs), with O(V) retained
memo/path storage. This does not optimize authenticated key-grant traversal or the
separate electorate commitment. Full-scale memory/latency qualification is open.

Differential tests cover all 625 four-node graphs, all 16 eligibility subsets,
depths 0..5 and both query orders against the unchanged depth-limited resolver.
They assert at most one edge selection per eligible node. A 1,000-owner shared tail
checks proposal scope precedence and exactly 1,002 lookups. A tally regression
checks intermediate versus owner direct votes, explicit key abstention/no-choice,
and duplicate electorate entries.

## Current pending-expiry selector: 165 LMDB and 41 node tests passed

CX07's pending-return branch now requests expired ordinary claims from a derived
origin-time index in the existing writer-generation cache. Cold reads stream the
primary pending table to build timestamp/key membership; warm reads reconcile
changed pending keys and fetch only due payloads. Selection restores primary-key
order before returning rows, preserving return processing order. The existing
first-provenance predicate and return_credit exclusion remain; empty provenance
never enters the index. The node keeps its defensive eligibility check.

Origin timestamps are indexed instead of period-specific deadlines, so governed
expiry changes and backward clocks use the same exact predicate with a new cutoff.
now == u64::MAX explicitly preserves Timestamp::has_expired's saturating-add rule.
Pending mutation/undo marks changed keys; checkpoint clearing invalidates the
index; restart/direct writes lose generation reuse. Errors poison the writer.
Cold index construction includes O(P log P) ordered-index work plus provenance
decoding; warm work depends on changed
keys and due rows, with primary-key sorting for the due set. Metadata is O(P);
no memory/workload or release claim is made.

## Candidate-balance expiry scan (137 library tests passed)

CX08 tracing confirms `refresh_token_counters` still scans the full portfolio even

Counter-cache design constraints confirmed from current code: revoked amounts
ignore expiry; all other states use effective-origin expiry, with saturating
addition at u64::MAX. A reuse entry must match portfolio storage identity and
expiry period, and time must remain between computation and next nonrevoked
expiry. Earlier timestamps require recomputation. Candidate mutation, rollback,
rule changes and externally restored roots must miss without relying on a TTL.
Use bounded derived metadata without retaining old token vectors, preserve checked
overflow errors, and keep direct full-scan comparison tests. The counter cache above has passed library and affected node integration validation.
